extracted.intended_audience: writers, rhetoricians, literary critics, and students of style (poets and orators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing 'the Sublime' in poetry and prose: definitions, sources, rhetorical figures, stylistic ornaments, and vices to avoid when aiming for lofty and moving language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sublime consists in a certain loftiness and excellence of language; it does not merely convince the reason but 'takes the reader out of himself.' It acts 'with an imperious and irresistible force' and 'sways every reader whether he will or no.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the primary evaluative test: does the passage lift the reader beyond ordinary judgment? A sublime passage can illumine an entire subject like a lightning-flash and produce immediate overwhelming effect rather than gradual approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachability: art versus native genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate whether sublimity can be taught: some claim it is born in a man and not acquirable by rule; Longinus argues that while the vital principle is from nature/genius, scientific method (art) can determine right degree and moment and train the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: judge both natural force and technical control. Writers should 'abandon themselves to the direction of their genius' while using art (knowledge of great models, practice) to regulate and refine inspiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandeur of Thought (first source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandeur of thought—nobility of soul producing elevated ideas—is a primary source of sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-criteria include: (a) nobility of soul as the source of great thought; (b) choice of the most striking circumstances; (c) amplification; (d) imitation of great models; (e) imagery. Evaluate whether thought itself is elevated, not merely ornamented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of striking circumstances / selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the most striking circumstances is part of producing grandeur of thought: choice and selection bring out the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the writer has chosen circumstances that magnify the idea; good selection often trumps mere ornamentation. 'Selection' is a central practical method to raise ordinary material into sublime expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplification—expanding on an idea or circumstance to heighten its effect—is listed as a means to produce sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of amplification to ensure it intensifies rather than dilutes the thought; compare examples (Plato, Demosthenes, Cicero) for effective amplification versus bombast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of great exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation (not slavish copying) of great models is a source of sublimity; writers should look to masterpieces as beacons and ask how Homer or Demosthenes would judge their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: does the writer learn by sympathy and emulation with past masters? 'Write for antiquity'—use the greats as judges to discipline taste and ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery and metaphors as source of Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery and well-chosen metaphors contribute to grandeur of thought and the Sublime (e.g., Sappho's ode is praised for striking circumstance and imagery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess aptness and force of imagery: metaphors should accumulate to produce elevation; beware of over-use or grotesque conceits. Appropriate, striking words are 'the very light of thought.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of moving the passions (second source)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sublime includes the power to move the passions—an ability to stir strong emotion in the reader (Longinus treats this separately elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether emotional appeal is genuine and proportionate to the situation. Distinguish true pathos from false sentiment or theatricality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of speech (third source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rhetorical figures (adjuration, rhetorical question, asyndeton, hyperbaton, changes of number/person/tense, periphrasis, etc.) are sources of Sublime when used effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mastery and concealment of art: the 'art to conceal art' is prized. Check individual figures for appropriateness and for their contribution to elevation rather than ostentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graceful expression (fourth source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Graceful expression—choice of words and ornaments of style (use of familiar words, metaphors, comparisons/similes, hyperbole)—is another source of Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate diction: are words chosen for power and appropriateness? Familiar words can be effective; metaphors should be accumulated judiciously. Prefer striking, apt words to mere prettiness or mannerism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of words / striking diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate and striking words have 'marvellous power and enthralling charm'—they are central to Sublime and 'the very light of thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge vocabulary for precision and force. Avoid mere word-tasting or flourish; prefer words that illuminate thought and move readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and elevation of structure (fifth source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural features—modulation of syllables, rhythm, and composition—contribute to dignity and elevation of a work and so to the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine sentence and clause structure, rhythmical modulation, and larger compositional arrangement. Structure should support and elevate thought rather than distract from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation of syllables and rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful modulation of syllables and rhythm is part of the elevated structure that aids sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rhetorical cadence and musicality: rhythm must be used to enhance effect, not abused. Avoid mechanical or forced rhythms that break the mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer Sublimity to tame correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Longinus counsels that Sublimity, even if imperfect, is to be preferred over tame correctness or faultless propriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: allow for grand faults when they arise from genuine force of thought; do not favor pedantic correctness over moral and imaginative greatness. However, distinguish genuine power from mere bombast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices opposed to Sublimity — bombast/affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bombast (affectation, grandiloquence) is a vice that 'transcends the Sublime' and becomes ludicrous; bulk that is hollow and affected produces an impression of littleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify grand phrases that produce absurdity rather than elevation (examples: 'curling torrent flames'). Penalize inflated diction that lacks genuine substance or feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puerility / frigidity / pedantry
rubrics_metrics.description: Puerility or frigidity—pedantic over-elaboration leading to paltriness and silly affectation—is a contrary vice to grandeur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge for over-refinement or artificial polish that extinguishes vigor. Avoid excessive prettiness, archaism, or minute technical display that undermines passion.

rubrics_metrics.name: False sentiment (ill-timed emotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: False sentiment: ill-timed, empty display of emotion or greater emotion than the situation warrants; tedious personal feeling unrelated to subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess emotional authenticity and appropriateness. Penalize plaintive or overwrought displays that leave readers cold or seem theatrical rather than sincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vices destructive to Sublimity (rhythm, clause, prolixity, anti-climax)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific vices listed as destructive: abuse of rhythm; broken and jerky clauses; undue prolixity; improper use of familiar words leading to anti-climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these surface defects as checklist items: excessive rhythmic trickery, choppy sentence construction, needless prolixity, and misapplied colloquial words/anti-climaxes all undermine sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and posterity as judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Longinus advises writing 'for antiquity' and posterity—asking what the great past masters would think and how future readers will feel—thus using broad, enduring judgment as a canon of sublimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate whether the work aspires to lasting greatness rather than fashionable cleverness. Writers should self-discipline by imagining the verdict of Homer, Demosthenes, or future readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral nobility as foundation of style
rubrics_metrics.description: Dignity and fire of style are traced to dignity and fire of soul; nobility of style is the 'bloom on nobility of soul.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the moral seriousness and sincerity behind rhetorical force. Sublimity that stems from genuine moral greatness is favored over technical bravura unbacked by character.

rubrics_metrics.name: The critic's methods: define subject and give methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A technical treatise should (1) define the subject and (2) point out how and by what methods writers may become masters of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a guide or pedagogical text, check for a clear definition of Sublime and practical, actionable methods (examples, exercises, models) to cultivate it.
